To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) insecticide-spraying interventions in Cochabamba had very strong, lasting effects on infestation rates; (b) the capital city, as well as municipalities with a larger proportion of dry forest habitat, had higher infestation rates; and (c) traditional strategies combining insecticide-sprays and longitudinal surveillance are very effective in highly endemic areas, and should be used in other parts of South America.
